rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of life — discovered by Hooke (1665), theorised by Schleiden, Schwann and Virchow, and limited in size by the surface-area-to-volume ratio. Every cell shares a membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes and DNA, but two great designs exist: prokaryotic cells (bacteria, cyanobacteria) keep their naked circular DNA in a nucleoid, have no membrane-bound organelles, use 70S…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
General size: prokaryote ~ 1-10 µm; eukaryote ~ 10-100 µm
Magnification = image size ÷ real size

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **"Prokaryotes have no nucleus" vs "no DNA":** prokaryotes have DNA — just no nuclear envelope around it. The nucleoid is DNA + cytoplasm, not a membrane compartment.  ·  **Viruses are NOT prokaryotes:** viruses are acellular (no membrane, no cytoplasm, no ribosomes); prokaryotes are complete living cells. This is also why viruses are exceptions to cell theory.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Cell theory exceptions is a rising favourite (asked 2024): memorise all four exception categories with one-line reasons.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Mycoplasma*** — smallest known cell (~0.1 µm), no cell wall, prokaryote.  ·  **Ostrich egg** — largest single cell (~15–18 cm).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **70S vs 80S:** the S (Svedberg) unit measures sedimentation rate, not size — 70S ribosomes are not "smaller than 80S by 10"; they differ in subunit composition (50S+30S vs 60S+40S).  ·  **Cell wall vs cell membrane:** every cell has a membrane; only some have a wall. The wall is outside the membrane, fully permeable; the membrane is the selective barrier.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Compartmentalisation** — membranes create internal environments so incompatible reactions coexist; the defining advantage of eukaryotic organisation.  ·  **Surface-area-to-volume limit** — the physical reason for cell size and multicellularity.  ·  **Selective toxicity** — 70S vs 80S ribosomes let antibiotics kill bacteria without harming human cells.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Cell = smallest structural + functional unit of life; unicellular organisms do everything with one cell.  ·  Discovery chain: Hooke (1665, dead cork, named "cell") → Leeuwenhoek (1674, living cells) → Brown (1831, nucleus) → Schleiden & Schwann (1838–39, theory) → Virchow (1855, cells from cells).  ·  Cell theory: (1) organisms made of cells, (2) cell = structural + functional unit, (3) cells arise from pre-existing cells. Exceptions: viruses, viroids/prions, coenocytes, mitochondria/chloroplasts.  ·  Cells are small because volume grows faster than surface area — diffusion would fail in a big cell.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Robert Hooke coined the word "cell" in 1665 (Micrographia).  ·  Prokaryotes appeared ~3.5 billion years ago; eukaryotes ~1.5–2 billion years ago.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** What are plasmids and why are they important? **Answer.** **Small, self-replicating circular DNA molecules** in prokaryotes, separate from the main chromosome.…  ·  **Short answer (2m):** What is a nucleoid? **Answer.** The **irregular, non-membrane-bound region** of a prokaryotic cytoplasm where the single **circular, naked DNA chromosome** lies — no nuclear envelope separates it from the cytoplasm, which is why transcription and translation can be coupled.  ·  **Long answer (5m):** Differentiate between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. **Answer.** | Basis | Prokaryotic cell | Eukaryotic cell | |---|---|---| | **Nucleus** | No nuclear envelope; **nucleoid** with naked circular DNA | True nucleus; double envelope, nucleolus, pores | | **Chromosomes** |…

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: **Human RBC** — ~7–8 µm, biconcave, loses nucleus at maturity to maximise O₂ carriage.  ·  ***E. coli*** — rod-shaped bacterium; nucleoid + plasmids; model prokaryote of genetics.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Why Start Biology With the Cell? Everything you study after this topic — tissues, organs, digestion, heredity, evolution — is built on one organising idea: **the cell is the smallest unit of life**. Nothing smaller than a cell is alive; everything alive is made of one or more cells.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Conceptual Understanding — What a Cell Actually Is ### 2.1 Definition and the essential idea A **cell** is the smallest, basic **structural, functional and biological unit** of all living organisms — a mass of cytoplasm bound by a membrane, containing genetic material and capable of independent existence and reproduction.…  ·  ## 3. Prokaryotic Cells — Life Before Organelles ### 3.1 Definition and who the prokaryotes are **Prokaryotes** (Greek *pro* = primitive, *karyon* = nucleus) are cells that **lack a true nucleus and any membrane-bound organelles**. Their genetic material lies naked in the cytoplasm in a region called the **nucleoid**.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Every cell has: membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes, DNA, same genetic code.  ·  Prokaryote: no nuclear envelope, no membrane-bound organelles, 70S ribosomes, naked circular DNA + plasmids, peptidoglycan wall, binary fission.  ·  Eukaryote: true nucleus + nucleolus, membrane-bound organelles, 80S ribosomes, histone-bound linear chromosomes, mitosis/meiosis.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Endosymbiotic theory explains mitochondria/chloroplasts: own circular DNA, 70S ribosomes, double membrane.  ·  Plant vs animal cells: wall, plastids, central vacuole, centrioles are the four standard differences.  ·  **Binary fission vs mitosis:** binary fission has no spindle, no chromosome condensation, no nuclear envelope breakdown — it is simpler DNA replication + splitting.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ***Anabaena*** — filamentous cyanobacterium; photosynthetic lamellae, heterocysts fix nitrogen.  ·  For "differentiate" questions, present a table with named bases; the 2021 paper asked for "any three points" — give exactly three well-labelled rows plus a fourth as safety.  ·  "The cell is not just a unit of structure — it is the unit of function, heredity and evolution."

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: "Eukaryotic success is the success of internal membranes."  ·  "Hooke saw dead, Leeuwenhoek saw living" — the discovery order.  ·  **Long answer (5m):** Describe the structure of a bacterial cell with a labelled diagram. **Answer.** **From outside in:** 1. **Cell wall — peptidoglycan (murein)**: rigid, gives shape and osmotic protection; attacked by lysozyme and penicillin. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Conceptual (3m):** "The eukaryotic cell is a compartmentalised cell." Explain. **Answer.** Membrane-bound organelles wall off **separate chemical environments** inside one cell: - **Lysosomes** hold acid hydrolases at **pH ~5** while the **cytosol runs at pH ~7.2** — the same cell hosts two incompatible chemistries…  ·  **Conceptual (3m):** Why do cells remain small even in large organisms? **Answer.** **Geometry and diffusion.** When a cell's linear size doubles, its **volume grows 8× (cube)** but its **surface only 4× (square)** — the surface-area-to-volume ratio falls.…  ·  **Application (3m):** A new antibiotic inhibits 70S ribosomes.
